metadata.story-title: Flush Orchestrator Buffer on Session End

story-context.problem-statement:
The agentic-memories orchestrator only flushes buffered messages when: 1. Batch size threshold reached (2+ messages), OR 2. A NEW message arrives 30+ seconds after the first buffered message
This means single messages or final messages are NEVER stored if: - User sends one message and leaves - User sends a message, gets response, and closes the app - User's last message before session timeout
Risk: Critical information (allergies, preferences, decisions) can be permanently lost.
Solution: Background polling worker that detects inactive sessions and triggers orchestrator flush with generous timeouts (5-min polling, 10-min inactivity threshold). This is a FALLBACK mechanism - most conversations have 2+ messages and batch normally.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Background worker runs every 5 minutes to check for stale sessions
Sessions inactive for 10+ minutes trigger orchestrator flush
Flush uses flush=true parameter via stream_conversation_message()
Flush happens asynchronously, doesn't block any user operations
If orchestrator unavailable during flush, log warning (graceful degradation)
Single-message conversations are stored within ~15 minutes of inactivity

implementation-approach.rationale: - Simple implementation, works with any Redis config, low overhead - Piggybacks on existing retry worker pattern in memory.py - Generous timeouts avoid false positives (5-min poll, 10-min inactivity) - This is a FALLBACK mechanism - most conversations batch normally

step.description: Add flush worker constants to MemoryManager
step.code: # Configuration constants (add to existing constants) FLUSH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 300 # 5 minutes between checks INACTIVE_THRESHOLD = 600 # 10 minutes of inactivity before flush FLUSH_MARKER_TTL = 3600 # 1 hour TTL for "already flushed" marker

step.description: Add flush worker to main.py startup event
step.code:
@app.on_event("startup") async def startup_event(): """Application startup handler.""" logger.info("Annie Backend API starting up...") # ... existing startup code ...
# Start background workers from api.memory import MemoryManager memory_manager = MemoryManager()
# Start retry worker for queued memories asyncio.create_task(memory_manager.start_retry_worker())
# Start flush worker for stale sessions asyncio.create_task(memory_manager.start_flush_worker())

scenario.steps: 1. Send one message to chat endpoint 2. Wait 15 minutes (10 min inactivity + 5 min poll cycle) 3. Check agentic-memories logs for extraction
scenario.expected: Message is extracted and stored as memory

scenario.steps: 1. Send 3 messages rapidly 2. Check agentic-memories logs
scenario.expected: Messages batch normally (2-3 extraction calls), flush worker not needed

scenario.steps: 1. Stop agentic-memories service 2. Wait for flush worker to run 3. Check backend logs
scenario.expected: Warning logged, no crash, graceful degradation

scenario.steps: 1. Trigger flush for a session 2. Wait for next flush worker cycle 3. Check logs
scenario.expected: Session marked as flushed, not flushed again

redis-keys.key: Session data with last_activity timestamp (TTL: 1 hour)
Marker that session was already flushed (TTL: 1 hour)

notes.note: This is a FALLBACK mechanism - most conversations have 2+ messages and batch normally
Generous timeouts (5-min poll, 10-min inactivity) to avoid false positives
Empty content with flush=True is sufficient to trigger orchestrator flush
The orchestrator's /v1/orchestrator/message endpoint already supports flush parameter
